title: Entanglement-Assisted Timing Optimization for Discriminating Amplitude-Damping Dynamics
authors: Massimiliano F. Sacchi, Milajiguli Rexiti, Stefano Mancini
abstract: We analyze minimum-error discrimination of two qubit dynamical processes generated by phase-covariant amplitude-damping Lindbladians in a single-use scenario. The optimization involves both the input probe, possibly entangled with an isolated ancilla, and the interrogation time. For unassisted probes we obtain a closed expression for the optimal trace-norm distinguishability at fixed time, with distinct interior and boundary branches. For entanglement-assisted probes, the common phase covariance of the two channels reduces the diamond-norm optimization to a one-parameter Schmidt family. The resulting formula gives transparent sufficient conditions for fixed-time entanglement advantage and separates this local advantage from advantage after global optimization over time. We exhibit examples in which the best unassisted strategy is approached only asymptotically, whereas an entangled probe achieves a strictly smaller error probability at finite time.
summary: This paper analyzes how best to discriminate between two noisy qubit processes undergoing amplitude damping by optimizing both the input probe state and the measurement time. It rigorously proves that using an entangled probe can yield a significantly lower error rate at any finite time compared to the best unassisted strategy, which only approaches this limit asymptotically.
main_problem: The study focuses on determining the minimum error probability for discriminating between two distinct qubit dynamical processes governed by phase-covariant amplitude-damping Lindbladians.
main_result: Entanglement assistance allows for a strictly lower minimum error probability at finite interrogation times compared to the best achievable unassisted strategy, which only approaches this value asymptotically.
method: The authors use quantum information theory tools, including trace-norm and diamond-norm distinguishability measures, optimizing over both the input probe state (including entanglement) and the interrogation time $t$.
model_or_system: The system involves two qubits undergoing dynamics described by a master equation representing phase-covariant amplitude-damping Lindbladians. The analysis is performed in a single-use scenario.
key_observables: Minimum error probability ($p_E, e_p$), optimal trace-norm distinguishability ($D_{	ext{sep}}(t)$), and entanglement-assisted distinguishability ($D_{	ext{ent}}(t)$).
important_parameters: The damping rates ($\gamma_+$, $\gamma_-$, $\gamma_z$) define the dynamics, and time $t$ is a crucial optimization variable.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the underlying dynamics are phase-covariant amplitude-damping semigroups; for entanglement assistance, it leverages common U(1) phase covariance to simplify the optimization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison of minimum error probabilities versus time, demonstrating finite-time advantages achieved by entangled probes over unassisted ones, and show threshold behavior for this advantage.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem setup using distinguishability measures. It then analyzes the unassisted case, deriving closed forms for optimal strategies on different branches. The core contribution involves showing how entanglement reduces the optimization to a one-parameter Schmidt family, leading to fixed-time and time-optimized advantage criteria.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous quantitative bounds on the resource utility of quantum entanglement in practical open-system measurements, distinguishing between static vs. time-dependent advantages for characterizing decoherence channels.
